summary: The Kepler conjecture: the arXiv abstract says This is the eighth and final paper in a series giving a proof of the Kepler…
body: The arXiv record https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9811078 for "The Kepler conjecture" abstracts the work as follows: "This is the eighth and final paper in a series giving a proof of the Kepler conjecture, which asserts that the density of a packing of congruent spheres in three dimensions is never greater than $π/\sqrt{18}\approx 0.74048...$. This is the oldest problem in discrete geometry and is an important part of Hilbert's 18th problem. An example of a packing achieving this density is the face-centered cubic packing. This paper completes the fourth step of the program outlined in math.MG/9811073: A proof that if some standard region has more than four sides, then the star scores less than $8 \pt$." This card quotes that abstract. A preprint is the authors' manuscript.
